Hi Emily / Carlos,

Thanks for a productive call today — great to meet the Finova team. As promised, here's a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps. Please confirm or correct any items below.

Summary of requirements (from today's discovery):
- Latency targets (p95): US < 200ms, EU < 250ms, APAC < 350ms
- Throughput: sustained 500 req/s across the fleet, peak bursts up to ~2,000 req/s
- Concurrency: expected per-user concurrency ~6-8 active streams
- Streaming: real-time streaming required for chat UI; target chunk latency < 50ms (client-visible)
- Regional routing: traffic should be routed to the customer region (US/EU/APAC) with automatic fallback to nearest region if local capacity is constrained.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU; APAC customers prefer APAC residency where available.

Open questions / clarifications we need from Finova:
1) Can you confirm the model family and sequence length assumptions for production (tokens per request average / max)? This will affect throughput/instance sizing.
2) Do you require guaranteed in-region processing (hard residency), or is a regional preference with documented fallback acceptable?
3) Are there specific SLA/uptime numbers you require beyond the latency targets?
4) Expected launch / peak traffic date (you mentioned Q3) — please confirm target week so we can propose capacity plans.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marissa to share SLO template + initial capacity calc (attached).
- Technical deep-dive with Aditya (Solutions Eng) to validate feasibility and sizing — propose 30–45 minute call.
- Security/compliance sync (DPA, data residency) — loop in your security contact and our compliance lead if needed.

Attachments: finova-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO template / initial numbers)

If the items above look right, can you confirm by EOD tomorrow and suggest 2 times for the technical deep-dive next week?

Thanks — look forward to moving this forward.
\Best,

Thanks for the ping, Marissa — looping in a concise technical take based on the numbers you provided. Short answer: yes, the targets are achievable with the right sizing and deployment mode. Details below.

High-level recommendations:
- Hosted with Dedicated Pools: For initial beta we can use Hosted API with reserved Dedicated pools (regional) to guarantee capacity. This meets latency and throughput targets with proper autoscaling/burst config.
- Dedicated / Private for hard residency: If Finova needs hard in-region processing (EU-only), recommend Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1 or Private deployment (customer VPC). Private gives the strongest contractual residency guarantee but has higher onboarding and support overhead.

Latency / sizing notes (T5-like, avg 400 tokens):
- p95 targets: With regionally pinned Dedicated pools we estimate p95 ~ 120–180ms (US), 150–230ms (EU), 220–320ms (APAC) depending on instance type and network. Suggested baseline: NVIDIA A10G or H100 (quantized) for production; H100 for highest throughput/dense concurrency.
- Throughput: To support 2k peak requests (avg 400 tokens) with streaming, we recommend a Dedicated pool sized to ~8-12 A10G-equivalent GPUs (or 4–6 H100 if available). We'll run a follow-up perf test with representative prompts to finalize.
- Concurrency & streaming: Streaming chunk latency <50ms is achievable if we: 1) use client-side small chunk sizes (e.g., 64 tokens), 2) enable our low-latency streaming path (bypass large-batch queues for streaming connections), and 3) reserve concurrency slots for realtime streams.

Fallbacks & routing:
- Smart routing: We can route by geo with strict preference for in-region endpoints and documented fallback rules when capacity is constrained. Fallback events are logged and auditable.
- Cache & batching: Prefix/KV caching reduces token work for repeated prompts; batching policies tuned per route preserve latency for realtime streams while batching non-streaming traffic.

Data residency / compliance:
- Hosted Dedicated with regional isolation can meet most residency needs (data at rest and processing in-region).
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) required for contractual hard-residency with no cross-region processing. We can provide DPA language and SOC2 artifacts (attached summary).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Schedule a 45-minute perf-sizing call with Finova engineering (Aditya + Neha + Finova eng) — propose Thu or Fri next week.
2) Share a short perf test plan and small set of representative prompts so we can run load tests in a sandbox region.
3) If Finova needs hard residency, have legal/security review DPA and propose Private vs Dedicated cost delta.

Attachments: finova-slo-matrix.xlsx (updated with SE notes), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Happy to jump on a call — propose Thu 2027-04-22 14:00 UTC or Fri 2027-04-23 10:00 UTC.
